audit.why: 56.05% over 3085 games, FAVOURED at 4/10, and the kit backs it: Xerath has no dash, blink or escape in any slot, so every stage where Fizz can reach him is a Fizz stage.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[5] and whys[6] are swapped — whys[5] sits on the First item row but argues the 2-item mark, and whys[6] sits on 2+ items but argues the first-item combo. whys[6] also credits Xerath with a shield he does not have.
audit.why: Nothing in Xerath's kit shields. His real late spike is Rite of the Arcane's 5000-unit range at a 130/115/100s cooldown, which pressures objectives rather than the duel.
audit.corrected: First-item row describes the first-item kill inside Shocking Orb's 11s window; 2+ row describes his global ult pressure.

audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer invents a 'Mage Armor rooted form' (spikes[0], wants.you[1]) and a Xerath shield (spikes[2], whys[6], wants.foe[1]). Neither exists. Shocking Orb is also called a root in spikes[2] when it is a stun. Separately, the page never states the one interaction that decides fights: Rite of the Arcane is a channel, so Chum the Waters' knockup cancels it outright. breakdown.cooldowns carries no digit (lint COOLDOWN_NO_DIGIT).
audit.why: Kit: P Mana Surge, Q Arcanopulse 9/8/7/6/5s at 750 range, W Eye of Destruction 14/13/12/11/10s at 1000, E Shocking Orb 13/12.5/12/11.5/11s at 1050 and flagged hardCC, R Rite of the Arcane 130/115/100s, flagged channel — 'immobilizes himself' — so any CC ends it. Fizz R is flagged knockup; Fizz E is untargetable on a 16/14/12/10/8s cooldown.
audit.corrected: Fabricated form and shield removed, stun named correctly, and the R-channel interaction stated in spikes[1], whys[4], mid and wants.you[1].

audit.whatIsWrong: The cooldowns field never says how long the stun is down.
audit.why: Shocking Orb barely scales — 13s at rank 1 and still 11s at rank 5 — so a dodged orb buys the same long window at every level. That is the concrete fact the field exists to carry.
audit.corrected: Written in with Arcanopulse's 9-to-5s poke clock and the 130s ultimate.

edits.before: - Xerath Shocking Orb (Stun): matchup-defining — His only CC — dodge the orb and his artillery never converts into a kill. It governs your forward steps. - E Playful / Trickster spent on poke is a death you scheduled. - Hold the R for the fight that decides something.
edits.after: - Shocking Orb (E): 13s at rank 1 and still 11s at rank 5 — it barely scales, so one dodged orb buys the same long window all game. - Arcanopulse (Q) falls from 9s to 5s; that is the poke clock. - Rite of the Arcane is a 130s channel and any CC ends it.

edits.before: Xerath has some of the best poke damage in the game from Arcanopulse but absolutely no mobility or escape, meaning that once you're in melee range on him the fight is essentially over. He'll try to chip your HP down from max range and root into his empowered casting form, but you can use minion waves and angles to close the gap safely and punish him hard for every cast he lands too close. Play patient early, then all-in the moment you get within E range.
edits.after: Xerath has some of the best poke damage in the game from Arcanopulse but absolutely no dash, blink or escape, meaning that once you're in melee range on him the fight is essentially over. He'll chip you from 750 range and hold Shocking Orb, 13s at rank 1, as his one answer, so use minion waves and angles to close and punish every cast he takes too close. Play patient early, then all-in the moment his stun is spent.

edits.before: Rite of the Arcane hits globally and adds to his poke pressure, but it does nothing to save him from a dive, so Playful/Trickster still lets you dodge his Arcanopulse and Shocking Orb before jumping on top of him during his rooted casting animation. He'll look to poke you down and use his ult for chip damage across the map, but as long as you close distance safely this phase remains firmly in your favour. Keep pressuring and punishing every overextension.
edits.after: Rite of the Arcane reaches 5000 units and adds to his poke, but it immobilizes him for the whole barrage, so it is a dive invitation: Playful/Trickster dodges Arcanopulse and Shocking Orb on the way in, and Chum the Waters' knockup ends the channel outright. He'll poke you down and chip the map with his ult, but every cast he takes at close range is a kill you get. Keep closing and punish every overextension.

notes: Level chart is all-Fizz across both layers and matches the packet levelChart and a 56.05% win rate, so no chart rows were moved and no paired win[N] edits were needed. Two fabrications were removed: a 'Mage Armor rooted form' (Xerath has no such ability) and a Xerath shield cited in three places. Whether Fizz's Playful/Trickster untargetable window makes an in-flight Shocking Orb whiff or merely delays it is not answerable from Riot's text, so I did not assert it anywhere. Report entries were left alone apart from none rewritten — the two lint-flagged fields were dosFull/dontsFull, not report[].
